mappings.note: What the king hid in the chest -- a specific point recovered from the narrative. Rejected LO-8, which is the skim-for-usefulness outcome.

The evidential basis for the eldest brother's guess (a light chest, something rolling) -- exactly a close examination of the text for the detail that carries the inference. Rejected LO-6: the author's idea is not under appraisal.
The basis for the middle brother's 'pomegranate' inference, located in the text. Rejected LO-8: a specific evidential detail, not the text's overall use.
On what the brothers' camel description rested -- observation of signs, found in the passage. Rejected LO-6: no agreement or disagreement is invited.
The brothers' resolve after their father's death -- plot detail. Rejected LO-8: not a gist item.
How the story ends -- located detail. Rejected LO-8: the ending is a fact, the moral is asked separately.
Why the horseman suspected theft -- the reason is stated in the narrative. Rejected LO-6: the learner reports the reason rather than judging it.
Meaning of the phrase 'paini drishti' -- fine grain of language and a new phrase. Rejected LO-9: the demand is lexical, not a search for a narrative point.
The king's words of praise -- a quoted specific point. Rejected LO-8: the praise is located, not summarised.
Hardships after forty days -- detail list from the text. Rejected LO-5: the hardships are narrated, not a local issue for the learner to react to.

How they described an unseen camel, answered at the level of 'insight and experience' -- a summary characterisation of the whole narrative method and what it is good for. Rejected LO-9: no single detail answers it.
The accusation laid against the brothers -- specific point. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
What the middle brother reported about the camel (blind in one eye). Rejected LO-8: a located detail.
Why the owner grew suspicious -- reason given in the text. Rejected LO-6: no evaluation asked.
Why the king sent for the chest -- the narrative states the purpose. Rejected LO-8: a point, not the text's usefulness.
How the youngest knew the fruit was unripe -- the evidential detail. Rejected LO-6: a found reason, not an idea to weigh.
Footprints in the sand as the basis for the woman-and-child inference. Rejected LO-8: specific evidence, not gist.
Grass cropped on one side only -- the detail that yields the one-eyed inference. Rejected LO-12: no lexical work involved.
What the king did on seeing their intelligence. Rejected LO-8: an outcome of the plot, not its lesson.
The brothers' defining quality -- a judgement about the whole tale and what it holds up for admiration. Rejected LO-9: no single point states it.
Blank is 'teen' -- opening fact of the tale. Rejected LO-12: no lexical difficulty.
Blank is 'mahal' -- setting detail. Rejected LO-12 for the same reason.
Blank is 'pag' in the collocation 'pag badhaana' -- the item turns on knowing the set phrase, not the plot. Rejected LO-9, used for the blanks whose missing word is an ordinary noun.
Blank is 'oont' -- plot detail. Rejected LO-12: plain vocabulary.
Blank is 'mantri' -- plot detail. Rejected LO-12 as above.
Blank is 'anaar' -- plot detail at the tale's reveal. Rejected LO-8: recall, not gist.
Blank is 'ghudsavaar' -- plot detail. Rejected LO-12: ordinary word.
Blank is 'pita'; 'chal base' is the euphemism but the blank is the plain noun. Rejected LO-12 on that ground.
The lesson the tale teaches -- its usefulness, read off the whole text. Rejected LO-9: no detail carries it.
Why the horseman took them for thieves -- reason stated in the text. Rejected LO-6: reported, not appraised.
The kind of wealth the poor man urged them to gather -- a located answer ('paini drishti aur teevra buddhi'). Rejected LO-6, which I keep for the item that also asks why that wealth matters.
What the brothers decided after the death -- plot detail. Rejected LO-8: not the tale's point.
Number of days travelled -- a single figure from the text. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
What they said was in the chest. Rejected LO-8: recall.
Grass cropped on one side -- the evidential detail behind the inference, in short-answer form. Rejected LO-6: no idea to agree with.
The king's order for the test. Rejected LO-8: a located instruction.
Why the king kept them at court -- the reason is stated. Rejected LO-8: a point, not the moral.
Which quality astonished the king -- named in the text. Rejected LO-12: the phrase is quoted, not glossed.
Who the youngest inferred were riding. Rejected LO-8: specific point.
The footprints the eldest saw -- the evidential detail. Rejected LO-6: no evaluation.
How the king set the test -- procedure recovered from the text. Rejected LO-8: not the tale's usefulness.
The three converging clues for the pomegranate -- close examination of the passage. Rejected LO-8: evidence, not gist.
Why the chest was placed by the door -- the narrative gives the king's motive. Rejected LO-6: reported, not judged.
Why the camel's owner took them for thieves. Rejected LO-6: the reason is in the text.
The advice received in childhood -- located detail. Rejected LO-6, kept for the item that also asks its justification.
What the king finally did -- a sequence of located facts. Rejected LO-8: not the moral.
The king's instruction to the camel owner. Rejected LO-8: bare detail.
How the brothers were honoured -- detail list. Rejected LO-8: the reward is a fact, not the lesson.
Hoofprints circling and halting -- the evidential detail behind 'he is searching for something'. Rejected LO-6: an inference the text supplies, not one to contest.
Why they set out and what plan they made -- two located details. Rejected LO-14: the plan is the characters', not the learner's own experience to write up.
The right-side grass eaten and the left untouched -- the precise evidential contrast. Rejected LO-8: detail, not usefulness.
Hardships on the journey -- detail list from the text. Rejected LO-5: narrated hardship, not an issue for the learner to respond to.
What the youngest reported and on what evidence -- both located. Rejected LO-6: no appraisal.
The first inference and the dust prints behind it. Rejected LO-8: specific evidence.

Asks both WHICH wealth the father urged and WHY -- the key argues that this wealth fills every lack, so the learner has to grasp and restate the author's proposition about wealth. Rejected LO-9, which I used for the items that only ask which wealth was named.
